features.name: Sign Up Context Parameter
features.description: A new parameter in the redirect URL that determines the origin of a sign up, such as whether it came from the Microsoft website (marked as viral) or from Shopify. It enables customized onboarding experiences based on customer context.
caveats: Currently only supports two scenarios: Microsoft website (viral) and Shopify
Must be URI encoded when included in redirect URL

features.name: Profiler Form on Website
features.description: A regular form built on your website that collects customer and prospect information through questions of different sorts, with full control over the website implementation and question types.
caveats: Requires careful construction of the sign up URL with specific elements for proper functionality

features.name: Sign Up Context JSON Key-Value Pairs
features.description: The sign up context can contain custom JSON key-value pairs that you define based on information collected from the profiler. Examples include interest (basic trade) and previous system preference (Excel). You determine what key-value pairs are included.
caveats: Certain key-value pairs are required when using an app ID
Must be URI encoded when included in the redirect URL

features.name: Sign Up Context Storage in System Table
features.description: The sign up context information is automatically stored in a system table inside Business Central. Apps can read this table during installation to recognize the sign up context and transfer relevant data to base application tables.
caveats: Developers must implement app logic to read and react to the stored sign up context
Data must be transferred to base application tables based on documentation requirements

features.name: App ID in Sign Up Context
features.description: You can specify an app ID in the sign up context to indicate which app should be automatically provisioned as part of the Business Central Standard trial. The app ID is public information available from your store listing.
caveats: App ID must be obtained from store listing
Country code must match both customer's AD tenant and app's supported countries

features.name: Country Code Validation in Sign Up Context
features.description: When using an app ID, the country code in the sign up context must match both the customer's Azure AD tenant country code and must be among the app's supported countries. Mismatches prevent app provisioning.
caveats: Three-way match required: customer AD tenant, app supported countries, and sign up context
Failures prevent app installation during provisioning

features.name: End User License Agreement Acceptance Flag
features.description: The sign up context must include an end user license agreement acceptance flag set to true. This ensures that apps are only provisioned if the user has explicitly accepted the app's EULA on your website.
caveats: Developers must provide users with access to the EULA before provisioning
API will not load the app if this flag is not set to true or EULA is not accepted

features.name: Checklist Customization Based on Sign Up Context
features.description: Apps can react to sign up context key-value pairs to load specific checklist items during provisioning. For example, if a user selected basic trade in the profiler, the app can load a checklist tailored to basic trade needs.
caveats: Requires app development to implement reactive logic
Depends on proper capture of profiler answers in sign up context
